Ground floor staff are very rude
2 floor staff are very corporate

It very sad operating lagging off knowledge lagging up care lagging  of everything Unprofessional, do not take your love one to this hospital.
Very good

Very frustrating

I brought my aunt to pick up medication on the 3rd floor. I was confused by the queuing system. They told us to sit on brown chairs for the medical history check, and then on orange chairs. We didn't know what they were for because the staff didn't explain. This was my first time there. After asking around, I learned that sitting on the orange chairs meant seeing the doctor, but they didn't specify where to start. Some people just added their own chairs to cut in line. So, those who had been sitting for a long time didn't realize they were being cut off, and those who came later didn't know they couldn't sit there and kept cutting in. The system might have problems, but they should at least put up some signs or instructions to explain how to wait. There was only a sign outside the doctor's room informing people to pick up their appointment slips before paying. The service on each floor is very strange, and this floor was the strangest I've ever experienced – a system of musical chairs. Those with good legs could get up and exercise, but those with disabilities suffered terribly.

However, once you understand the system, it's okay. Having seats is good, especially for the elderly.

I appreciate the clear queuing system with seats, which prevents cutting in line, unlike the 2nd floor where standing is tiring and people are constantly being cut in line. As soon as they opened an additional lane, I hurried to the end of the line to get my appointment slip before people who had been standing there for almost half an hour, or even 45 minutes.

The service from the staff was extremely toxic and mentally unstable. The system was terrible. Nurses were loud and rude, even when I asked questions because I didn't know the answer. The person screening was incredibly sharp-tongued, acting like they weren't at fault at all. I paid over 3,600 baht for a health checkup, but received incredibly toxic service from the staff. It was like I was asking for a free checkup. The staff were so rude, it was like they forgot they were there to provide care.

The problem stems from the terrible system. After leaving the examination room, one person told me to go pay. When I went to pay, the finance department told me to ask the nurse about the cost of the tests. When I asked the nurse, she yelled at me, saying I should have gone to the counter before the examination (how would I know? I'm a patient, not a staff member, I wouldn't know the procedures!). When I went to pay and asked for my appointment slip to attach to my work because I was on leave, they told me to ask the nurse. When I asked the nurse, she yelled at me, telling me to ask the finance department. The mental health of the staff was utterly toxic.

The service is friendly and family-like. All examination rooms are clean.
The waiting area is very clean. The nurses provide excellent service in every room you need to visit. The restrooms are also clean and always maintained by staff.

📢 Booking a dental appointment online is very convenient, hassle-free, and fast. It saves a lot of money. The doctor and assistants are lovely. At the scheduled time, you go up to the 4th floor, weigh yourself, have your blood pressure checked, and confirm your appointment. I usually arrive about 15 minutes early, or about an hour early, to have my blood pressure checked again because I have high blood pressure and need it measured multiple times. Almost everything was perfect.
❌ Except for some male doctors who, seeing that a case was difficult, refused to treat it. They went on to treat teeth that weren't specified, even though my medical history clearly indicated which teeth needed treatment (1, 2, 3, 4). This caused the patient to have to reschedule.
✅ I wondered if this doctor might not be as skilled as I thought, and I can confidently say this because I've encountered this twice with this male doctor. This is based on my personal experience receiving treatment at this hospital. I hope that others who go for treatment will receive the most lovely doctors and assistants. 🙏🙏🙏

I went to the dental department and waited in line for a very long time. I had to find the doctor. The doctor examined me for less than 3 minutes, ordered an X-ray, and then informed me that I needed this or that treatment. Then, they told me to schedule a follow-up appointment for a tartar removal first. I was stunned, wondering if that was all for today. The doctor said that the examination was the end of the day's work. I had been waiting in line since 7 am. The examination took less than 5 minutes, and I went home without getting the tartar removed. That's the kind of service I received. Just sharing my experience.
author_name: สิรินลินพร บุญพิมพ์

text: I've been receiving treatment at this hospital for a long time; both my daughters were born here when it was in the old building. Today, I went to pick up medication for my mother and encountered a female doctor on the second floor, room 2, who displayed terrible behavior. She spoke rudely and gave me an extremely condescending look. I hope the hospital director will provide some training for her. This happened around 9:00 AM. I don't know what the problem was.
author_name: สิริทิพย์ พอกพูลขำ

text: On January 5th, 1969, I went to the doctor because I had fallen and gotten a large wound on my knee. The doctor sent me for a tetanus shot and wound treatment at a new procedure room outside the building. I arrived, placed my form, and waited. After a while, a nurse came out and said it was closed and would reopen at 1 PM. The sign outside said it was closed from 12:00-13:00. It was 11:40 AM at the time. I was told patients had to wait outside in the hot sun, and my wound was painful, but the nurse said it was closed even though it wasn't the scheduled time on the sign. In the end, I couldn't wait any longer and went to a private clinic, paying more and wasting an hour waiting.

Prior to my visit, I contacted the hospital to inquire about Shockwave Therapy and was informed by the Physical Therapy department that such a service was available. I then proceeded to the hospital as instructed.

However, upon arrival and informing the nurse/staff (4th floor) of my request, I received an inappropriate response. The staff used inappropriate language and tone, including making jokes and inquiring about the size of my genitals. This made me feel uncomfortable, disrespected, and violated the standards of medical service expected.

While I understand that taking a medical history is part of treatment, it should be done politely, professionally, and with consideration for the patient's feelings, especially regarding sensitive issues.

Therefore, I kindly request that the hospital consider improving its staff's service guidelines to prevent similar incidents from happening to patients in the future.

I received treatment for high blood pressure and cholesterol from Dr. Phung on the 4th floor. The staff were excellent, polite, and very helpful. Dr. Phung was also very kind and gave me good advice. I've been receiving treatment here for 2 years now. The 4th floor is clean and the air conditioning is cool.
author_name: สมทรง เกษตรผลจํารูญ

text: This was my first time using Bang Yai Hospital for prenatal care using my universal healthcare coverage. I want to say that all the staff – nurses, doctors, finance staff, pharmacists – were incredibly kind. It was nothing like the reviews I read beforehand. I had prepared myself for anything negative, but my experience was completely different. Sometimes, some staff might be a little loud, especially when communicating with foreigners who might not understand, requiring repetition and clarification. However, when speaking to me or others, it was perfectly normal. I was very impressed! You really have to experience it yourself to truly understand. The only downside was the long wait for the doctor's appointment because it was so busy, and I was one of the last in line. I will add more reviews if I have any further comments, as this was my first time there.
author_name: นันทพร ช้างเผือก (อ๊ะออย)

text: The chronic disease clinic on the 3rd floor, room 5, doctor: The doctor was uncommunicative, didn't prescribe all the necessary medication, and when we reported that our mother was coughing a lot, the doctor said, "She's not coughing right now. She doesn't look like she's sick." Does she mean we have to wait until the symptoms appear before coming to see her? She coughs a lot in the evenings, but not in the mornings. The doctor's attitude was terrible. Is this all the doctors the hospital has? Are they so used to treating patients like this that they think they're clueless? If it's just a matter of prescribing the same medication, the nurses could do it. Or hire a doctor who is caring and genuinely wants to treat patients. A doctor who makes patients feel lucky to have met them. They didn't even inform us if they forgot to give or stopped medication. When we tried to go back to ask, they were gone. We asked the reception staff, but they couldn't do anything. The queuing system is completely disorganized. The hospital has been around for a long time, but there's been no improvement at all. It's heartbreaking for patients who have to be treated here.

Terrible! The clinic provided incorrect information to the patient. They told the patient the sutures were dissolvable, but almost a month later, they were still there. Upon checking the patient's medical records, it was found that the …

I brought my grandfather to the clinic on the 3rd floor, and the queuing system is terrible. They're calling out numbers skipping ahead. When we went to inquire, they said we'd already been called. We sat there listening as our numbers were skipped. For example, we were queue number 210, but the nurse called 209, then 211. When we asked, they just said, "We've already called you. What time?" Just saying so wouldn't be so bad; system errors happen. But the way they spoke and looked at us was like they didn't want to serve us, especially since we were there for their services. And this is a hospital, so the service should be more comfortable, but instead, it was very frustrating. To add, I wasn't the only one who got skipped; 4-5 people in front of me experienced the same thing.

The dental clinic on the 4th floor is clean and provides good service. It's convenient to come outside of regular hours; you can schedule an appointment between 3:00 PM and 3:30 PM, with the first patient starting at 4:00 PM. It's very clean. I use my government welfare benefits and social security; fillings are free. Thank you to the doctor and staff for the excellent service.

I had the opportunity to use the services of Bang Yai Hospital, in the special room on the 4th floor. The room looked nice, but the waiting area didn't clearly indicate who could sit there and which seats were reserved for patients only. Someone unfamiliar with the hospital might see an empty chair and sit there while waiting for a patient relative. Then a male staff member would tell them to move if they weren't being examined. Why not put up clear signs or have staff to guide people? Instead of acting so aggressively, how would anyone know? People who haven't been there before might see an empty chair, and it wasn't even right in front of the examination room door; it was on the opposite side, and there was no sign prohibiting non-patients from sitting there. You're the one who didn't put up a sign prohibiting non-patients from sitting there, so how can you blame us? Please improve your communication and attitude to be more positive and avoid a negative experience that causes a bad feeling.

The maternity ward service was terrible. They made us press the emergency button and wait for hours, only to find out the button was broken and they wouldn't let us open the door. The staff there were rude and didn't follow any instructions. When we asked when we could go home, they just told us to wait and didn't give any updates.

Bang Yai Hospital provides terrible service. The doctors, nurses, and all staff are very rude and lack professionalism. They are selective about which patients they accept. A patient arrived at the emergency room at night, and they were told they wouldn't be admitted. The hospital refused to treat a patient who wasn't seriously ill. It's baffling. How do they know which patients' conditions aren't serious? Think carefully before considering going there. It's unacceptable. I wouldn't even give it one star.

It's really bad today. I got hit by a car and then I went around 6:30. The person who came to take care of the matter in front of me was really rude. Did he not want to take care of the matter or something? He acted like he was dissatisfied. Did he not want the job anymore? I'm sorry for being rude. It's really disgusting. If you're dissatisfied and don't want to do it, just resign. 7/12/25

Today I went for a health checkup with my father and consulted him about a lump on his eye. The doctor and nurses were very kind and took great care of us. However, the person screening us had a very rude attitude. Please address this. Their speech was terrible. I called to speak with a nurse who was easy to understand, but the screening staff just kept saying "no, no." When I tried to get them to speak with a nurse, they refused. It was a very unpleasant experience.

I gave birth at this hospital. On the day I went, I met a nurse who was a bit chubby, wore glasses, and had a high-pitched voice. She was the one who delivered my baby. During a very intense labor, when I was pushing, the nurse told me to …

The staff at the registration counter on the first floor called out one number too late. When I asked if my turn had passed, they told me that if it was busy, I should get a new queue number. I was confused, wondering if it really had to be that way, especially since they didn't call my number when it was my turn, and the queue number screen wasn't even on. They just called past me. The staff member was also very rude. If you're going to explain things to patients, you should speak more politely. This needs improvement. It was a terrible experience.

Everything has been incredibly slow since 10:50 AM. It's now 1:42 PM and we haven't even been called in for a medical history interview.
The hospital needs to acknowledge that everything is extremely slow.
We brought three children for checkups, and if everything is going to be this slow, please find additional treatment options or streamline the system.
Please have some consideration for the patients waiting for their examinations.
This is considered the largest hospital in the district.

text:
The problems at this hospital lie in its OPD system management and communication.

The OPD system, which starts at the registration counter, creates a bottleneck. Even scheduled patients have to present their appointment cards at the registration counter, leading to overcrowding until their turn is called.

Personally, I experienced paperwork issues stemming from the hospital's back-end, resulting in me being moved to the back of the queue despite submitting my card earlier.
The patient management system is disorganized; I constantly had to ask what to do next and if the process was complete. Fortunately, the front-line staff were somewhat helpful and able to resolve some problems.

Waiting times for appointments were inconsistent. The hospital stated my appointment was at 9:00 AM, but I waited for three hours, until noon, before being sent for lunch and told to return in the afternoon to wait again before being seen. If the queues were separated into 9:00 AM, 10:00 AM, and 11:00 AM, they should calculate the average time required per patient and provide a more accurate estimate so patients have time to manage their schedules and avoid congestion at the OPD.

Payment and medication dispensing were not a problem.

It's been 10 years since I last visited Bang Yai Hospital, and it's changed a lot.
The doctors, nurses, and staff provide excellent care and service. …

Today I visited Dr. Pongsakorn's dental clinic. He provided excellent care and advice. He couldn't fill my tooth, but he did a teeth cleaning (tartar removal) for me. It was covered by my social security benefits, so there was no charge.

text:
Arrived at 7:30, left around 9:40. Just checked in for an appointment and waited for the appointment slip...oh my, it took so much time...

They've improved.
The dentistry on the 4th floor is clean and the service is good. It's convenient to come outside of normal hours.
You can get an appointment from 3:00 PM to 3:30 PM. The first appointment starts at 4:00 PM. Very clean. I use state welfare benefits and social security.

The service was better than expected. I was admitted using my universal healthcare coverage. It might not be as comfortable as a private hospital,

but the equipment and facilities were complete and up to standard.

I only paid an additional 2,100 baht per night for the room.

The process is simple, few steps, staff are knowledgeable and can answer questions (though their tone might be a little firm), and fellow patients are friendly. Sometimes, asking patients or their relatives is also helpful.😝 …

The staff at the registration counter on the 6th floor were extremely rude. If they're not ready to provide good service, they should quit. There was only one woman, a young woman, who seemed forced to work there. All the other staff were polite.

All the nurses working in the incision ward are very caring and attentive. I received wound care for almost a month (using the 30-baht health insurance, a continuation from a hospital in a provincial area). They observed my wound daily when I had it cleaned, notifying me of any improvement or worsening. If anything seemed abnormal, they would advise me to see a doctor again.
After my second visit, the medication and treatment method were changed as the nurses had pointed out. However, I would like to see a fast track option for immediate wound examination by a doctor if any abnormalities are detected. Based on the observations made by the nurses in the incision ward, this would prevent the need to queue again to see a doctor and have the wound cleaned the next day, as the waiting time is very long. This would allow for immediate adjustments to the treatment method. I understand there is a shortage of personnel. Nonthaburi has the highest population, but I would like the hospital management to address this issue.
I would also like to see if the number of hospital beds and personnel are sufficient for the population so that additional personnel can be added to alleviate the current staffing levels and reduce waiting times for patients to see doctors. I believe this will allow the hospital to develop faster and more modern treatment methods.

Normally, the service is good, but today, the management of the queue for x-rays was terrible. I asked to take my place in the queue, but they switched. They had studied x-rays before and took my place in every 3-4 queues. It was the worst. I came to pay for it myself, not to use it for free.

I used the insurance department to purchase health insurance cards for migrant workers. A chubby, blonde-haired staff member took over around noon. The service was poor, and in the end, I didn't buy the cards. Another issue is that the …

text: This doctor is terrible. I took a family member to get a disability certificate, and the doctor didn't fill in all the information. They should hire a better doctor, not just someone who wants to get it done quickly. The document is …

This was my first time at this hospital for a medical check-up for a job application. I was very impressed with several things:
1. There's a lot of parking space because there's an empty area next to the hospital where you can park. There are also quite a few food stalls (but no shade).
2. The medical check-up wasn't as crowded as I expected. I arrived at the hospital around 7:30 AM. After opening my medical record (which was very easy; just inserting my ID card to verify my identity and handing it to the staff), I waited in front of the specialist clinic on the 4th floor. I put the pink slip I received in the basket and waited. The nurse arrived around 8:30 AM. I was then called in to have my blood pressure taken, my medical history taken, and then sent for various lab tests specified by the company. Mine included a blood test, a urine test, and an X-ray.
At the lab, upon arrival, I scanned the barcode on the pink slip and received a queue number (but I recommend informing the staff again beforehand that you also need a urine test). The queue for blood tests didn't take long at all. It might be because it wasn't a medical check-up. I only waited a short time before getting my turn for blood and urine tests. After that, I went to the 3rd floor for an x-ray.
Then I came back to the 4th floor to wait for the results.
The whole process flowed quite smoothly. There was no waiting around except for the lab results. Once the lab results were out, they called me in to see the doctor to hear the results, receive the medical certificate, and pay. All of this only cost 550 baht.
I finished paying at 10:40 AM, so it only took about 3 hours in total. That's very fast for me considering it's a government hospital, because I was mentally prepared to wait 5 hours, haha.
3. All the staff were very nice. No one was rude or aggressive, even though I didn't know anything about what to do or where to go. I was especially impressed with the nurse in the special clinic.

The emergency room nurse spoke very rudely, even though there weren't many patients—only one or two in fact. I don't know what she was so tired of, but she took her frustration out on the patients and their relatives, even though we were …

I was initially shocked by the reviews, fearing poor service, but my personal experience was far from disappointing. This district-level government hospital excels in cleanliness, service, patient queuing management, and screening—better than many provincial-level hospitals. The nurses provide excellent advice and ask detailed questions about symptoms. The outpatient waiting area is air-conditioned and comfortable. For a government hospital to manage things at this level is outstanding.

text: I wanted to send my support to the nurses in the delivery room on the 5th floor of the outpatient building. And thank the doctor who delivered my baby. My baby was in a breech presentation (the doctor was so kind; I had a follow-up appointment for my C-section wound, and the doctor greeted me, remembered me, asked about the baby, inquired about the baby's condition, and even gave me advice on wound care). I was so impressed and grateful. I had booked a private room, but the baby was born with rapid breathing and needed oxygen. The baby needed close contact with doctors and nurses, so I chose to stay with him in the shared delivery room. However, I got to see how attentive all the nurses were to me and my baby. While waiting for the baby's blood test results, I requested to be moved to a private room because the baby could initially be taken off the oxygen machine. Also, the baby's father and relatives wanted to visit and see the baby. So, I gained experience with both shared and private rooms at Bang Yai Hospital. The private rooms are just rooms, nothing special. Checking on the baby was very superficial; for example, weighing the baby – in the shared delivery room, they weighed him without clothes (how attentive they were!), but in the private room, they only weighed him without the swaddling cloth. The weight difference was significant. The doctor assessed the baby and said he could go home without any concerns, just waiting for the blood test results in the afternoon. When I asked at the counter about the private room, the nurse said I could stay another night to wait for the results. But I felt it was wasteful because it was just like sleeping without any check-ups or care, and I wanted to go home because the doctor assessed me in the morning and said there was nothing wrong, so I could leave that day. However, when I told the nurse at the counter, she sounded displeased and had a displeased expression. I would like to see improvements in the private rooms. Everything else was great from my prenatal care to childbirth. Thank you from the bottom of my heart. 🙏🏻
I went to see the doctor after hours, received a quick examination, and was able to get medication to take home quickly. Thank you very much!
I brought my grandmother for an eye exam.
